summary: Audit application-layer authorization across API routes: service-role bypass, IDOR, authz-helper coverage, input validation
logs: 4 finders over 135 routes (32 service-role) + authz helpers, read-only

confirmed.title: goals/save trusts client-supplied profileId as the write key — cross-tenant overwrite of financial goals & strategic plans
confirmed.evidence: The auth gate (lines 63-96) verifies the caller against `businessId` only (owner / assigned_coach / super_admin / any business_users membership of businessId). It then computes `const saveProfileId = profileId || businessId` (line 101) where `profileId` is an unvalidated, client-supplied field from the request body (destructured line 54, schema `profileId: z.string().optional()` line 16). `saveProfileId` is used verbatim as `business_id` for every subsequent SERVICE-ROLE (RLS-bypassing, `admin = createServiceRoleClient()` line 61) write: business_financial_goals upsert onConflict business_id (lines 120,176-178), strategic_initiatives insert/upsert/delete (lines 287,300,340,383), sprint_key_actions (line 405) and operational_activities (line 459). Nothing checks that `profileId` belongs to `businessId`. Schema confirmed: business_financial_goals.business_id and strategic_initiatives.business_id both FK→business_profiles, so a victim's business_profiles.id is a valid target. A logged-in client (owns their own business → passes the gate for their own businessId) can POST {businessId: <own>, profileId: <victim business_profiles.id>, data:{financial:{...}}} and the `onConflict:'business_id'` upsert OVERWRITES the victim's entire financial-goals row, and inserts attacker-authored strategic initiatives / sprint actions / operational activities under the victim's business. Only the KPI branch is safe (it re-resolves from businessId via resolveBusinessProfileIds, line 201). Requires knowing the victim's profile UUID (leaks via reports/URLs/the resolve-business endpoint).
confirmed.remediation: Do not accept profileId from the client as a write key. Derive it server-side from the already-authorized businessId via resolveBusinessProfileIds(admin, businessId) (already imported and used for KPIs), or, if a profileId is passed, verify profile.business_id === businessId before use. Reject the request on mismatch.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed reachable cross-tenant write. In src/app/api/goals/save/route.ts the auth gate (lines 64-96) authorizes the caller ONLY against client-supplied `businessId` (owner/assigned_coach/super_admin/any business_users membership). Line 101 then sets `saveProfileId = profileId || businessId`, where `profileId` is a separate, unvalidated client field (raw body line 54; schema `z.string().optional()` line 16 — no UUID check, no check that it belongs to businessId). `saveProfileId` is used verbatim as the `business_id` write key for every service-role (RLS-bypassing, createServiceRoleClient line 61) write: business_financial_goals upsert onConflict 'business_id' (lines 120/176-178), strategic_initiatives insert/upsert/delete (287/300/383), sprint_key_actions (405), operational_activities (459). Only the KPI branch re-derives via resolveBusinessProfileIds (201) and is safe.

Schema verified against prod (read-only): business_financial_goals.business_id FK -> business_profiles AND has a UNIQUE constraint on business_id, so onConflict:'business_id' performs a real cross-tenant UPDATE/overwrite of a victim's existing financial-goals row; strategic_initiatives.business_id FK -> business_profiles. A victim's business_profiles.id is therefore a valid, overwrite-capable target.

Concrete path: any authenticated user who owns/belongs to any single business passes the gate with businessId=<own>, then POSTs profileId=<victim business_profiles.id> and data.financial/initiatives to overwrite the victim's financial goals and inject attacker-authored strategic initiatives/sprint actions/operational activities under the victim's business. DB RLS does NOT block this — the service-role client bypasses RLS, so the weak app-layer check is the sole and defeated gate (independently exploitable, not a DB-protected paper cut).

Severity stays HIGH, not CRITICAL: exploitation requires knowing the victim's business_profiles.id, a non-enumerable UUID (leaks via reports/URLs/resolve endpoint but is not default-available). That unmet-by-default condition is exactly the HIGH criterion (a known id required). Matches the finder's HIGH rating; not downgradeable below HIGH because no auth/RLS backstop exists once the UUID is obtained. Remediation is correct: derive profileId server-side from the authorized businessId via resolveBusinessProfileIds, or verify profile.business_id === businessId before use and reject on mismatch.

confirmed.title: team/remove-member never checks that memberId belongs to the authorized business — cross-tenant member removal & account deletion (IDOR)
confirmed.evidence: canRemove (lines 50-75) authorizes the caller against the client-supplied `businessId` (owner/assigned_coach/super_admin/business_users admin of businessId). But the member is then loaded and deleted by `memberId` ALONE, with a SERVICE-ROLE client: `.from('business_users').select('user_id').eq('id', memberId).single()` (lines 78-82) and `.from('business_users').delete().eq('id', memberId)` (lines 96-99). There is NO predicate tying memberId's row to businessId. Schema confirms business_users.id is a standalone PK (business_users.business_id FK→businesses, unrelated to the id used here). So an owner/admin of their OWN business A passes businessId=A to satisfy the gate, then supplies memberId = any business_users.id from victim business B, and that row is deleted — evicting the victim's team member. The only owner-protection is `if (memberUserId === ownedBusiness?.owner_id)` (line 91), which is business A's owner, not B's. With `deleteCompletely:true` (lines 106-152), if the victim user has no other business_users rows, the route also hard-deletes them from system_roles, public.users, and auth.users via the Admin API — full cross-tenant account destruction. Requires a known business_users.id (UUID).
confirmed.remediation: Scope the member lookup and delete to the authorized business: add `.eq('business_id', businessId)` to both the select (line 78-82) and delete (line 96-99), or fetch the member first and 403/404 if member.business_id !== businessId before any delete.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against src/app/api/team/remove-member/route.ts and the live schema. The route (POST, withSchema-wrapped) has a session gate (lines 28-32) and an authorization gate (lines 50-75) that computes canRemove against the CLIENT-SUPPLIED businessId — caller must be super_admin, or assigned_coach/owner/business_users-admin of that businessId. But the member is then loaded and deleted by memberId ALONE on the service-role client (RLS bypassed): line 78-82 `.from('business_users').select('user_id').eq('id', memberId).single()` and line 96-99 `.delete().eq('id', memberId)` — neither has `.eq('business_id', businessId)`. Schema confirms business_users.id is a standalone uuid PK with a SEPARATE nullable business_id column, so memberId and businessId are uncorrelated at the DB layer, and RLS does not intervene because every query uses adminSupabase (service/secret key). The owner-protection at line 91 (`memberUserId === ownedBusiness?.owner_id`) checks business A's owner, not the victim business B's, so a non-owner member of B is deletable. Concrete reachable exploit: an authenticated owner/admin of their own business A sends businessId=A (satisfies canRemove via isOwner) plus memberId = any business_users.id from victim business B; canRemove passes, the guard passes, B's member row is deleted (cross-tenant eviction). With deleteCompletely:true and the victim in no other business, it cascades to system_roles, public.users, and auth.users via the Admin API — full cross-tenant account destruction. RLS provides NO backstop here (service-role throughout), so there is no downgrade on that basis. The only precondition is knowledge of a valid, opaque, non-enumerable victim business_users.id UUID, plus the attacker owning/admin/coaching at least one business of their own (every real customer qualifies). That "needs a known id" condition is precisely the HIGH boundary (a service-role write with weak authz gated by a known id), not CRITICAL (which requires no unmet condition). Original HIGH rating is correct. Actor: any-authenticated-user (business owner/admin/coach) with a known victim member id.

confirmed.title: subscription-budgets trusts the GLOBAL coach role + uses the service-role client, bypassing RLS for cross-client read/write
confirmed.evidence: authoriseBusinessAccess() falls back to a GLOBAL role check: `if (roleData?.role === 'coach' || roleData?.role === 'super_admin') { return { ok: true } }` (line 845/152 region) — it never scopes the coach to `assigned_coach_id` of the requested business. All GET/POST/DELETE data access then runs through the module-level service-role client `const supabase = createClient(URL, getSupabaseSecretKey())` (line 42), which BYPASSES RLS. So any user whose system_roles.role='coach' can pass ANY business_id/forecast_id and read, upsert, or delete another client's subscription_budgets. RLS on subscription_budgets is scoped to auth_get_accessible_business_ids() (assigned-coach only), but the service-role client ignores it entirely. Contrast cfo/flag-client and monthly-report/generate which DO scope coach→assigned_coach_id. Latent today (system_roles has exactly 1 coach) but a real cross-client hole the moment a second coach exists.
confirmed.remediation: Replace the global coach branch with an assigned-coach check: after resolving the business, require biz.assigned_coach_id === user.id for the coach path (mirror cfo/flag-client lines 60-66), or route reads/writes through verifyBusinessAccess() which already scopes coach per-business. Keep super_admin as the only global bypass.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at HIGH. Every load-bearing claim verified in code. (1) route.ts:42-45 builds a module-level service-role client via getSupabaseSecretKey(); all three handlers (getHandler L174, postHandler L255, deleteHandler L304) execute their read/upsert/delete through it, so RLS on subscription_budgets is fully bypassed and the app-layer authoriseBusinessAccess gate is the ONLY isolation control. (2) authoriseBusinessAccess at route.ts:146-154 grants { ok: true } to ANY user whose system_roles.role is 'coach' or 'super_admin', with NO comparison to the requested business's assigned_coach_id — a coach can supply an arbitrary business_id/forecast_id and read, upsert, or delete another tenant's subscription budgets. (3) This deviates from the canonical verify-business-access.ts, which scopes coaches to assigned_coach_id (L22,L41) and reserves the global bypass for super_admin only (L71).

Adversarial checks: session gate IS present (getUser() at L86 → 401), so this is not unauthenticated-reachable and not CRITICAL. RLS does NOT backstop the weak check because the queries run on the secret-key client. A normal client-role user (21 of them) hits the 403 at L156, so it is not any-logged-in-user exploitable. Prod system_roles shows exactly 1 coach + 2 super_admin today, so the single coach (effectively the platform owner with fleet-wide access) causes no cross-tenant leak now; the hole goes live the moment a SECOND coach is onboarded assigned to a subset of clients — that coach could read/write ALL clients' subscription_budgets via this route. That unmet condition (a second coach existing) is exactly the task's HIGH criterion, and the concrete reachable path holds, so it is neither CRITICAL nor a downgrade below HIGH.

Concrete exploit (any-coach-cross-client): coach-role user calls GET|POST|DELETE /api/subscription-budgets?business_id=<victim tenant> → passes the unscoped role==='coach' branch (route.ts:152) → service-role client (route.ts:42) performs the operation on the victim's rows, RLS bypassed. Remediation as written is correct (require biz.assigned_coach_id === user.id for the coach path, or delegate to verifyBusinessAccess(); keep super_admin as the sole global bypass).

confirmed.title: consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId] PATCH lets ANY coach retag ANY forecast's tenant via the service-role client
confirmed.evidence: requireCoachOrSuperAdmin() (lines 35-58) only checks system_roles.role in ('coach','super_admin') — no per-business/per-forecast ownership check. The write `adminDb.from('financial_forecasts').update({ tenant_id: normalized }).eq('id', forecastId)` (lines 146-149) uses the service-role client `adminDb` (line 27), bypassing RLS. forecastId is any UUID from the path. A second coach could PATCH the tenant_id of a forecast belonging to another coach's client, corrupting that client's consolidation/budget math. No assigned_coach scoping anywhere in the handler.
confirmed.remediation: Load the forecast's business_id, resolve dual-ID, and verify the caller is the assigned coach (or super_admin) before the update — or perform the update through an auth-bound client so RLS applies. The sibling consolidation/businesses/[id] route already does the owner/assigned_coach `.or()` scoping; apply the same here.

verdict.reasoning:
The code defect is real and accurately described. In src/app/api/consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId]/route.ts, requireCoachOrSuperAdmin() (lines 35-61) enforces ONLY a global role gate (system_roles.role IN ('coach','super_admin')) with no per-forecast/per-business ownership scoping, and the mutation at lines 146-149 (`adminDb.from('financial_forecasts').update({ tenant_id: normalized }).eq('id', forecastId)`) runs through the service-role client (lines 27-30), fully bypassing RLS. The sibling route consolidation/businesses/[id]/route.ts DOES scope via owner_id.eq/assigned_coach_id.eq (requireAccess, lines 90-102), confirming the intended pattern this route omits. RLS provides no compensating protection here because the service key bypasses it.

However, the concrete cross-tenant exploit path ("any coach retags ANOTHER coach's client forecast") requires a second coach that does not exist. Prod system_roles: client=21, coach=1, super_admin=2. With a single coach on a single-coach fleet, that coach crosses no tenant boundary, and the 2 super_admins are trusted to administer any business by design across every consolidation route. No currently-reachable principal can perform a cross-client write. Thus there is no proven current cross-tenant path — the gap is latent, becoming exploitable only the moment a second non-super-admin coach is provisioned. Impact is also narrow and reversible (mutates a single tenant_id field, not data read/exfiltration).

Verdict DOWNGRADE, corrected severity MEDIUM (missing object-ownership authz / defense-in-depth on a service-role write, no proven current cross-tenant path). The remediation is still valid and should mirror the businesses/[id] route: load the forecast's business_id, resolve dual-ID, and verify assigned_coach_id/owner_id (or super_admin) before the service-role update. Re-rate to HIGH immediately if a second coach account is ever added. File: /Users/mattmalouf/Desktop/business-coaching-platform/src/app/api/consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId]/route.ts:146.

confirmed.title: consolidation/tenants/[connectionId] PATCH lets ANY coach edit ANY xero_connections row (service-role, no business scoping)
confirmed.evidence: Role gate is global: `if (role !== 'coach' && role !== 'super_admin')` (line 56), and the file header explicitly states 'No business-ownership check at this layer — any coach/super_admin is trusted with any connection.' The write `adminDb.from('xero_connections').update(validation.value).eq('id', connectionId)` (lines 106-109) uses the service-role client (line 30) so RLS is bypassed. connectionId is any UUID from the path. A second coach could rename, reorder, change functional_currency, or toggle include_in_consolidation/is_active on another client's Xero connection — cross-client write affecting FX translation and which orgs feed the consolidated numbers.
confirmed.remediation: Resolve the connection's business_id (xero_connections.business_id is businesses-space) and require the caller be that business's assigned coach or super_admin before updating. Do not trust the global coach role for a per-connection mutation.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at HIGH. The PATCH at src/app/api/consolidation/tenants/[connectionId]/route.ts:106-109 executes adminDb.from('xero_connections').update(validation.value).eq('id', connectionId) on the service-role client (route.ts:30-33, built with getSupabaseSecretKey()), which BYPASSES all RLS — there is no DB backstop, so the app layer is the sole guard. That guard, requireCoachOrSuperAdmin (route.ts:38-64), only verifies a session (getUser, line 46) and a GLOBAL role of 'coach' or 'super_admin' (system_roles, line 50-56). connectionId is any path UUID (line 91). No code resolves the connection's owning business (xero_connections.business_id, businesses-space) or checks the caller's assignment to it; the file header (lines 14-16) states this explicitly.

This is a genuine authz gap, not by-design: the codebase's own verifyBusinessAccess (verify-business-access.ts:22,41) proves coaches are meant to be scoped per business via assigned_coach_id, and this route ignores that model, trusting the coach role globally.

Adversarial verification of the concrete path:
- Not CRITICAL. The role gate blocks regular users — prod has 21 'client' accounts, none of which can reach the write — so there is no unauthenticated or any-authenticated-user path.
- Write surface is bounded but harmful. The DB write uses validation.value from validateTenantPatchPayload (admin-guards.ts:108-183), a strict 5-field allowlist (display_name, display_order, functional_currency, include_in_consolidation, is_active); the route's Zod .passthrough() body is NOT what reaches the DB, so there is no arbitrary-column write or privilege escalation. But toggling is_active/include_in_consolidation or changing functional_currency on another client's Xero connection corrupts that client's consolidation/FX translation — a real cross-client integrity write.
- Latency condition. Prod has 1 coach + 2 super_admin. super_admin has global access by design (verify-business-access.ts:71), so those two cross no boundary; with a single coach there is no adversary because that coach legitimately manages all clients. The cross-tenant exploit becomes live the moment a SECOND, scoped coach is onboarded — that coach could edit connections of businesses assigned to a different coach.
- RLS does not downgrade it: service-role bypasses RLS, so nothing caps this to MEDIUM at the DB layer.

This lands exactly on the HIGH rubric: a service-role write with weak/no authz that needs the second-coach condition to be independently cross-tenant. Remediation stands: resolve the connection's business_id and require the caller be that business's assigned coach (or super_admin) before updating; do not trust the global coach role for a per-connection mutation.

confirmed.title: subscription-budgets: service-role reads/writes/deletes gated only by a GLOBAL coach check (any coach reaches any client's budgets)
confirmed.evidence:
The route builds its DB client with the SECRET key at module scope (line 42-45: `const supabase = createClient(NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, getSupabaseSecretKey())`) so every GET/POST/DELETE query BYPASSES RLS. The only authorization is `authoriseBusinessAccess(businessId)`, whose coach branch is unscoped:
  line 146-154: `const { data: roleData } = await sb.from('system_roles').select('role').eq('user_id', user.id)...; if (roleData?.role === 'coach' || roleData?.role === 'super_admin') { return { ok: true, userId: user.id } }`
There is no `assigned_coach_id === user.id` predicate — ANY user whose system_roles.role='coach' passes for ANY client-supplied `business_id`. The handlers then read/upsert/delete `subscription_budgets` filtered only by `.eq('business_id', businessId)` on the service-role client (GET line 174-177, POST upsert line 255-258, DELETE line 304-307). Contrast the correctly-scoped coach check in goals/save (line 75: `const isCoach = business.assigned_coach_id === user.id`) and verifyBusinessAccess (line 22/41). Prod has 1 coach today so it is latent, but a 2nd coach (or any future coach account) can read AND overwrite AND delete every other client's vendor/subscription budget by iterating business_id. A plain 'client' role cannot reach the branch (owner/team checks are correctly scoped), so this is coach-only, not any-authenticated.
confirmed.remediation: Replace the global role check in authoriseBusinessAccess with a per-business predicate: for a coach, require `businesses.assigned_coach_id === user.id` for the resolved businessId (mirror goals/save line 75 or call verifyBusinessAccess(user.id, businessId)). Keep the super_admin global bypass. Since the data ops run on the service-role client, this app-layer check is the ONLY tenant boundary — it must scope the coach.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at HIGH. Every load-bearing claim verified against the actual code.

1. RLS is bypassed for all data ops. src/app/api/subscription-budgets/route.ts:42-45 builds a module-scope client with the SECRET key (`createClient(NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, getSupabaseSecretKey())`). That `supabase` const is what the handlers use for the GET read (line 174-178 `.from('subscription_budgets').select('*').eq('business_id', businessId)`), the POST upsert (line 255-261, onConflict business_id,vendor_key), and the DELETE (line 304-307 `.delete().eq('business_id', businessId)`). Service-role bypasses RLS, so `authoriseBusinessAccess` is the ONLY tenant boundary on this route — the DB-layer RLS hardening cannot back it up.

2. The coach branch is global/unscoped. authoriseBusinessAccess (line 84-157) resolves the businessId, checks owner (line 128, correctly scoped), team membership (line 133-143, correctly scoped to resolvedBusinessId + user.id + active), then falls through to a role check: line 146-154 `select('role').from('system_roles').eq('user_id', user.id)... if (roleData?.role === 'coach' || roleData?.role === 'super_admin') return { ok: true }`. There is NO `assigned_coach_id === user.id` predicate — any user whose system_roles.role='coach' is authorized for ANY client-supplied business_id (either id-space). All three verbs (GET/POST/DELETE) call this same gate (lines 171, 227, 301).

3. This is a genuine deviation from the codebase's own model, not the intended design. The scoped coach pattern is used everywhere else: verifyBusinessAccess checks `business.assigned_coach_id === userId` (verify-business-access.ts:22 and :41) and only grants a GLOBAL bypass for super_admin (:71); goals/save uses `isCoach = business.assigned_coach_id === user.id`; coach/clients/[id]/forecast and /goals both gate on `business.assigned_coach_id !== user.id` unless super_admin. So per-business coach scoping is the platform's intended authorization model, and this route breaks it.

4. A plain 'client' cannot reach the hole: the owner and team-membership branches are correctly scoped, so an ordinary authenticated client of business A cannot read business B. The exploit is coach-only.

5. Exploitability today = latent. Prod system_roles: 1 coach, 2 super_admin, 21 client. The sole coach is the platform owner, who legitimately has fleet-wide access; super_admin's global bypass is by design. So there is no malicious actor who can exploit this at present — the concrete cross-tenant path (a coach iterating business_id to read/overwrite/delete every other client's subscription/vendor budgets) opens the moment a SECOND coach account is created, which is a routine, expected event for a coaching platform.

Severity stays HIGH, not CRITICAL: the cross-tenant read/write/delete is real and the code path is concrete, but it requires the unmet condition of a second coach existing (rubric: "same but needs a condition — a second coach existing" AND "a service-role write with weak authz"). Not downgraded to MEDIUM because there is no RLS backstop (service-role bypasses it) and the write path (upsert/delete of another client's budgets) is fully reachable — the only thing standing between latent and live is one INSERT into system_roles. The finder's HIGH rating and remediation (replace the global coach check with a per-business assigned_coach_id predicate / call verifyBusinessAccess, keep super_admin global) are correct.

confirmed.evidence: authoriseBusinessAccess() falls through to `if (roleData?.role === 'coach' || roleData?.role === 'super_admin') return { ok: true }` (line 152) — a GLOBAL role check, not scoped to businesses.assigned_coach_id. confirmed.title: consolidation tenant + forecast mutation routes trust the global coach/super_admin role with no per-business scoping (service-role writes to any client's Xero connection)
confirmed.evidence: requireCoachOrSuperAdmin() only checks system_roles.role in ('coach','super_admin') globally (route header comment: "No business-ownership check at this layer — any coach/super_admin is trusted with any connection"). PATCH then does service-role `adminDb.from('xero_connections').update(validation.value).eq('id', connectionId)` (line ~86) with only a UUID-format check on connectionId — no verification the connection belongs to the coach's assigned client. Editable fields include is_active and include_in_consolidation, so a second coach could deactivate/alter another coach's client's Xero connection (breaking their sync). Same pattern in consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId]/route.ts (global-coach gate, no assigned_coach/owner check). fx-rates routes share the gate but operate on global reference data so are not cross-client.
confirmed.remediation: After the role gate, resolve the connection's owning business and require the caller be its assigned_coach_id (or super_admin) before the service-role update; apply the same per-business scoping to consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId].

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at HIGH. Both consolidation mutation routes are exactly as described. src/app/api/consolidation/tenants/[connectionId]/route.ts:84-109 and src/app/api/consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId]/route.ts:77-151 gate on requireCoachOrSuperAdmin() which checks only system_roles.role IN ('coach','super_admin') GLOBALLY — no assigned_coach_id / business_users / owner scoping (the route header even documents this: "No business-ownership check at this layer — any coach/super_admin is trusted with any connection"). Both then write via adminDb, the service-role client (createClient with getSupabaseSecretKey(), route.ts:30-33 / 27-30), which BYPASSES RLS — so the coarse role gate is the ONLY protection; the freshly-hardened DB RLS does not cover this path. The target id (connectionId / forecastId) gets only a UUID-format check (line 91 / 84), no verification it belongs to the caller's client. tenants PATCH mutates is_active / include_in_consolidation / functional_currency etc.; forecasts PATCH rewrites tenant_id — both cross-client-impacting.

Reachability (prod-verified via SELECT on system_roles): 21 client, 1 coach, 2 super_admin. All 21 client users hit the 403 role gate — no regular logged-in user and no unauthenticated caller can reach the write. Therefore NOT CRITICAL. The cross-client write requires a SECOND coach intended to be scoped to only their assigned clients; today coach/super_admin are global trusted operators (effectively one coach + platform admins = Matt), so the any-coach-cross-client path is LATENT, not currently exploitable by any untrusted party.

Severity stays HIGH: it fits the rubric's HIGH definition on two explicit counts — a service-role write with weak/no authz, AND a cross-tenant write that needs a condition (a second coach existing). It is the write-side analog of lead AUTHZ-01. Not downgraded below HIGH because it is a genuine RLS-bypassing service-role write with zero object-ownership/per-business scoping; not raised to CRITICAL because the role gate blocks all 21 client users today. Remediation as the finder states: after the role gate, resolve the connection's / forecast's owning business and require caller == assigned_coach_id (or super_admin) before the adminDb update.

mediumLow.title: Per-business endpoints grant access on the GLOBAL 'coach' role instead of assigned_coach_id — any coach can reach any client
mediumLow.evidence: Multiple per-business routes authorize a caller whenever their system_roles.role === 'coach', with no check that the coach is the business's assigned_coach_id. forecast/[id] GET line 109 and DELETE line 225 (`isCoachOrAdmin = roleData?.role === 'coach' || 'super_admin'`); same global-coach pattern in forecast/[id]/recompute:109, forecast/seed-from-prior:104, forecast-wizard-v4/generate:91, annual-plan:57, actions:63, forecasts/export:79, subscription-budgets:152, and the cfo/* routes (flag-client:47, report-status:102, summaries:146). Contrast the CORRECT scoped pattern used elsewhere: goals/save, goals/resolve-business, requireSectionPermission, and the monthly-report/consolidated/* routes all gate coaches on `assigned_coach_id === user.id`. Today there is effectively one coach so this is latent, but it becomes a live cross-client read/write hole the moment a second coach exists. These routes use the RLS-bound createRouteHandlerClient() (not service-role), so DB RLS is the backstop — the severity depends on whether the hardened RLS policies also grant coaches global access; if they mirror this app check, RLS does not cap it.
mediumLow.remediation: Replace the global `role === 'coach'` grants with an assigned-coach check (assigned_coach_id === user.id) for the specific business, e.g. route everything through verifyBusinessAccess or requireSectionPermission which already do this. Keep super_admin as the only global role.

mediumLow.title: goals/save membership fallback omits the status='active' filter
mediumLow.evidence: The business_users fallback in the auth gate queries `.eq('business_id', businessId).eq('user_id', user.id).maybeSingle()` (lines 86-91) with no `.eq('status','active')`. A deactivated or pending member of businessId therefore still passes and can perform the service-role writes. verify-business-access.ts and requireSectionPermission both correctly require status='active' (the C-34 fix); this route was not updated to match. Impact is limited to a business the user was previously a member of (not itself cross-tenant), so LOW — but it compounds AUTHZ-SR-01.
mediumLow.remediation: Add `.eq('status','active')` to the membership fallback, matching verifyBusinessAccess and requireSectionPermission.

mediumLow.title: activity-log/login POST writes user_logins for an arbitrary client-supplied business_id
mediumLow.evidence: After auth (getUser), the POST upserts into user_logins with `business_id` taken directly from the request body (line 45) using a SERVICE-ROLE client (line 39), with no verification that the caller has any relationship to that business. The row is keyed on the caller's own user_id, so the only effect is polluting an arbitrary business's login-activity view with the attacker's own user_id/timestamp — no data disclosure (the GET path at line 104 uses the RLS-bound client). Defense-in-depth gap only.
mediumLow.remediation: Verify the caller has access to business_id (verifyBusinessAccess) before the service-role upsert, or derive the allowed business set server-side.

mediumLow.title: PostgREST .or() filters built by template interpolation — reviewed, not exploitable
mediumLow.evidence: All interpolated .or()/in filter strings were traced to non-attacker-controlled values: the monthly-report/*, forecasts/*, consolidation/businesses/[id], and goals/route.ts filters interpolate `user.id` (a Supabase-auth UUID, not user-settable); coach/client-completion (lines ~248-256) interpolates ownerIds/profileIds/businessIds that are all server-derived from the coach's own assigned_coach_id businesses; the Xero callback/complete-connection .or() (callback:64, complete-connection:149) interpolate ids from server-side pending records / OAuth state resolved to UUIDs. No route interpolates a raw request query/body string into a filter without it being a session-derived UUID first, so PostgREST filter-injection is not reachable. Noted for defense-in-depth: prefer .in([...]) arrays or UUID-validate before interpolation.
mediumLow.remediation: Optional hardening: UUID-validate any id before string-interpolating it into .or(), or use the array form (.in()) which parameterizes values.

mediumLow.title: Global coach-role fallback (broader than RLS's assigned-coach scope) in several forecast/plan routes
mediumLow.evidence: A repeated pattern grants access on the GLOBAL role rather than the assigned coach: `const isCoachOrAdmin = roleData?.role === 'coach' || roleData?.role === 'super_admin'` — forecast/[id] GET line 110 and DELETE line 226, forecast/[id]/recompute line 109, forecast/seed-from-prior line 104, forecast-wizard-v4/generate line 91, forecasts/export line 79, and annual-plan line 57. Unlike verifyBusinessAccess (which checks businesses.assigned_coach_id for THIS business), these accept any coach. Impact is currently CAPPED because these handlers do their data reads/writes through the auth-bound createRouteHandlerClient (RLS), and the RLS policies scope coaches to auth_get_accessible_business_ids() = assigned_coach_id only (confirmed against prod pg_policies on financial_forecasts / business_kpis). So a rogue/second coach is still blocked at the DB — but the app-layer intent is wrong and it would become a live cross-client hole if any of these routes were switched to a service-role client (as subscription-budgets already is).
mediumLow.remediation: Replace the global coach test with an assigned-coach check (businesses.assigned_coach_id === user.id) or call verifyBusinessAccess(), keeping super_admin as the only global role. Standardize on one helper so the app layer matches the RLS scope.

mediumLow.title: withSchema/withQuerySchema run in OBSERVE mode by default — Zod validation is not enforced at runtime
mediumLow.evidence: withSchema/withQuerySchema only reject when isEnforced(routeId) is true, which requires process.env.ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES to contain the routeId or '*' (lines 30-38, 60-73). Default (unset) = observe mode: a parse failure just logs a Sentry 'zod:would-reject' and the handler runs with the raw request anyway. So the Zod schemas wrapping ~100+ routes provide NO runtime guarantee — a malformed/oversized/wrong-type id or param reaches the handler unchecked. This is not itself a cross-tenant hole (every sensitive handler re-checks auth and does its own null/typeof guards, and ids are used in parameterized PostgREST .eq() filters, not string SQL), but it means the validation layer the codebase advertises (Phase-47) is inert unless the env var is set. Could not confirm ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES value in prod (secrets not in context).
mediumLow.remediation: Confirm ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES='*' is set in prod (or enforce per-route for the id-bearing routes). Until then, treat every handler's own input validation as the only real gate and keep UUID_REGEX-style checks on path/query ids (as consolidation/* already do).

mediumLow.title: PostgREST .or() filters built by template interpolation — reviewed, no attacker-controlled unvalidated value reaches them
mediumLow.evidence: Interpolated .or() filters were audited: monthly-report/generate:80, monthly-report/consolidated*:115/124/126, forecasts/export:68, forecasts/scenarios:80, consolidation/businesses/[id]:94, goals/route.ts:45 all interpolate the SESSION user.id (a trusted UUID from supabase.auth.getUser()). Xero/callback:64 and Xero/complete-connection:149 interpolate a business id, but that value is HMAC-signed OAuth state (verifySignedOAuthState) / a DB-stored pending_xero_connections.business_id respectively, not raw client input, and access is verified first. No route was found where an unvalidated, attacker-supplied request value is interpolated into a filter string, so PostgREST filter-injection is not reachable. Noting as a hardening item only.
mediumLow.remediation: Defense-in-depth: UUID-validate any id before interpolating it into an .or() string (the consolidation/* routes already gate on UUID_REGEX first — adopt that everywhere), or use the array/builder form instead of template strings.

mediumLow.title: activity-log/login GET reads user_logins by client-supplied business_id with no app-layer access check
mediumLow.evidence: getHandler authenticates but then runs `supabase.from('user_logins').select('*').eq('business_id', businessId)` (lines 107-108) with no verifyBusinessAccess/ownership check on the client-supplied business_id. However it uses the auth-bound createRouteHandlerClient and prod RLS on user_logins is `user_id = auth.uid()` (confirmed via pg_policies), so the query only ever returns the caller's OWN login rows regardless of the business_id passed — no cross-tenant leak. The POST path upserts via the service-role client but pins user_id: user.id, so a user can at most record their own login against an arbitrary business_id (data-integrity noise, not a cross-tenant read/write).
mediumLow.remediation: Add a verifyBusinessAccess(user.id, businessId) gate to the GET for consistency and to make the endpoint's intent (per-business login history for admins/coaches) actually work rather than silently returning only self-rows; validate business_id on the POST before the upsert.

mediumLow.title: consolidation/fx-rates writes are coach-global on shared FX data (service-role)
mediumLow.evidence: Role gate is global coach/super_admin (line 50) with the service-role adminDb for writes. fx_rates are platform-global exchange-rate rows, not per-client financial data, so this is not a per-tenant data-isolation leak — but a second coach could alter FX rates that feed every multi-currency client's consolidation (Dragon/IICT). Low sensitivity, noted for completeness alongside the other coach-global consolidation routes.
mediumLow.remediation: If fx_rates should be super_admin-managed only, tighten to super_admin; otherwise document that coaches share global FX config. No per-tenant scoping applies since the table is not business-keyed for the rate rows.

mediumLow.title: Global 'role === coach' fallback repeated in 5 per-business finance routes (RLS-capped today, but wrong pattern)
mediumLow.evidence: Five per-business routes grant access to ANY coach at the app layer instead of scoping to assigned_coach_id: forecast/[id] GET line 109 (`isCoachOrAdmin = roleData?.role === 'coach' || 'super_admin'`) and DELETE line 225; forecast/[id]/recompute line 109 (`isAdmin = roleRow?.role === 'super_admin' || roleRow?.role === 'coach'`); forecast/seed-from-prior line 103-104; forecast-wizard-v4/generate line 91; annual-plan line 57. UNLIKE subscription-budgets, all five perform their business/forecast reads and writes on the AUTH-BOUND client (createRouteHandlerClient), so RLS applies. I verified RLS scopes coaches correctly: financial_forecasts/businesses/business_financial_goals policies gate on `auth_get_accessible_business_ids()`, whose definition unions only `businesses WHERE assigned_coach_id = auth.uid()` (plus owner/team/super) — a non-assigned coach's row read returns 0 rows and the handler 404/403s BEFORE the global-coach branch matters. So the branch is unreachable-as-a-bypass today. It is still the wrong pattern (defense-in-depth that would become a live hole if any of these routes were switched to a service-role client, as subscription-budgets was).
mediumLow.remediation: Standardize on verifyBusinessAccess(user.id, businessId) (which scopes coach to assigned_coach_id) for all five, deleting the inline global `role === 'coach'` fallback. This removes the latent footgun and makes the app layer independently correct rather than relying on RLS.

mediumLow.title: Section-permission gate ships in LOG_ONLY mode — section_permissions.finances=false is not enforced
mediumLow.evidence: `SECTION_PERMISSION_ENFORCE = process.env.SECTION_PERMISSION_ENFORCE === 'true'` (default false). enforceSectionPermission (line 51/68) returns null (route proceeds) whenever ENFORCE is off, only emitting a Sentry event. Every finance route that calls requireSectionPermission (forecast/[id], forecast/seed-from-prior, forecast-wizard-v4/generate, monthly-report/*, etc.) therefore does NOT actually block a business_users member who has `section_permissions.finances === false`. requireSectionPermission itself is correct (auth-bound client, coach scoped to assigned_coach_id, active-members only, super_admin via system_roles) — the gap is purely that its deny verdict is advisory in prod. Impact is WITHIN-tenant (a restricted member of a business seeing that business's finances), not cross-client, so severity is low. Note also verifyBusinessAccess (used by the monthly-report family) grants any active member regardless of section_permissions, so even flipping ENFORCE would not restrict members on those routes without also consulting section perms there.
mediumLow.remediation: Confirm SECTION_PERMISSION_ENFORCE is intended to stay false; if section-level restriction is a real requirement, set it to 'true' after reviewing the LOG_ONLY Sentry signal, and ensure the monthly-report routes consult section permissions (not just verifyBusinessAccess membership).

mediumLow.title: requireSectionPermission called with a business_profiles.id (wrong id-space) in forecast DELETE — false-deny only
mediumLow.evidence: requireSectionPermission is documented to take `businesses.id` and internally does `.from('businesses').select('owner_id').eq('id', businessId)`. In the DELETE handler the call passes `forecast.business_id` (line 235), which the same file's comments state is a business_profiles.id (GET handler resolves it to businesses.id at line 63-82 and passes the RESOLVED businessId at line 128 — DELETE does not). When a profile-id is passed, the owner/coach/admin lookups all miss and the verdict is not_a_member (allow:false). Because enforce is LOG_ONLY this is inert today; if ENFORCE is turned on it would wrongly DENY legitimate owners/coaches on forecast DELETE. It can only fail closed (deny), never false-allow, so it is not a security hole — it is a correctness/availability latent bug and a dual-ID inconsistency.
mediumLow.remediation: In the DELETE handler resolve forecast.business_id to businesses.id (reuse the GET handler's resolution, or resolveBusinessProfileIds) before calling requireSectionPermission, matching the GET path (line 128).

mediumLow.title: Xero/sync-all POST lets any authenticated user trigger a sync for ANY business or the entire fleet (no object-level authz)
mediumLow.evidence: postHandler (line 73) only checks getUser() at line 75, then: `if (allBusinesses) { const results = await runSyncForAllBusinesses() ... }` (line 84) and `const result = await syncBusinessXeroPL(businessId)` (line 91). businessId/all come straight from `request.json()` (lines 81-83) with NO verifyBusinessAccess / assigned_coach / ownership check. Every other Xero route (status/disconnect/reactivate/sync/pending-connection/connection-health) re-validates business_id against owner_id/assigned_coach_id/super_admin; this one does not. syncBusinessXeroPL/runSyncForAllBusinesses run service-role writes into xero_pl_lines. A logged-in client can POST {"all":true} to force a sync of all ~18 tenants, or {"businessId":"<any-uuid>"} to force a sync of another client's business.
mediumLow.remediation: Gate postHandler the same way the sibling Xero routes do: resolve businessId and require owner_id/assigned_coach_id/super_admin via verifyBusinessAccess before syncBusinessXeroPL; restrict the all=true fleet path to super_admin only.

mediumLow.title: withSchema/withQuerySchema run in observe-only mode fleet-wide — invalid input is logged, never rejected
mediumLow.evidence: Enforcement requires the route id (or '*') to be present in process.env.ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES (isEnforced(), line 33-42). That env var is not set anywhere in the repo (.env*, vercel.json, code all clean), so for all 134 wrapped routes the parse-failure branch only does Sentry.captureMessage('zod:would-reject') and then `return handler(request, ...rest)` with the raw, unvalidated request (lines 63-73). Schemas are also `.passthrough()`. Net: the Phase-47 validation layer provides zero input rejection in production — every handler receives arbitrary input. No proven cross-tenant path because the audited handlers independently re-resolve ids and enforce authz, but any security property assumed to be guaranteed by a schema (enum/number/shape constraints before a privileged query) is currently unenforced.
mediumLow.remediation: Set ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES (at least to the privileged/service-role routes, or '*') in the Vercel production env, or flip the wrapper default to enforce. Confirm current prod value; if already set this downgrades to INFO.

mediumLow.title: PostgREST .or() filters built by raw template interpolation — safe today (values are session/DB-derived), but not UUID-guarded
mediumLow.evidence: Every interpolated .or()/filter reaches the query as a template string. All interpolated values are trusted: the majority are the session `user.id` (e.g. monthly-report/consolidated*, forecasts/scenarios line 80, consolidation/businesses/[id] line 94, goals/route line 45) which is a server-issued UUID; the two business-id cases interpolate server-derived values, not raw request input — Xero/callback line 64 `.or(\`id.eq.${businessId},business_id.eq.${businessId}\`)` uses a businessId recovered from the signed+verified OAuth state, and Xero/complete-connection line 149 uses `bizId` read from the pending_xero_connections DB row. token-manager line 894 interpolates a timestamp. No attacker-controlled, unvalidated value reaches a string filter, so PostgREST filter-injection is not reachable. Flagged only as defense-in-depth: these business-id values are not UUID-validated before interpolation.
mediumLow.remediation: Prefer parameterized filters (.eq/.in) over string .or() for id lookups, or assert UUID_REGEX on businessId/bizId before interpolation (the pattern already used in consolidation/tenants/[connectionId]).

result.synthesis:
# WisdomBI — Application Authorization Layer Audit (Final)

## 1. Executive verdict

**The application authorization layer is mostly sound but NOT independently correct.** The dominant, correct pattern is present: per-business routes derive identity from the session, scope coaches to `assigned_coach_id`, check the right ID-space, and require `status='active'` membership (`verifyBusinessAccess`, `requireSectionPermission` both verified correct). Cron routes all carry the fail-closed CRON_SECRET gate. Every non-public route calls `getUser()` first. No unauthenticated cross-tenant path exists.

**The single worst thing: two service-role IDOR write holes reachable by ANY authenticated user today** — `goals/save` (AUTHZ-SR-01) and `team/remove-member` (AUTHZ-SR-02). Both pass an auth gate against a client-supplied `businessId`, then perform the actual RLS-bypassing write keyed on a *different*, unvalidated client id (`profileId` / `memberId`) that is never checked to belong to the authorized business. These are not gated behind the hypothetical second coach — any of the 21 client users who owns/belongs to one business can, with a victim's opaque UUID, overwrite another client's financial goals and strategic plan, or delete another client's team member (and with `deleteCompletely:true`, cascade to full auth-account destruction). The only barrier is knowledge of a non-enumerable UUID, which is why they are HIGH not CRITICAL — but there is **no RLS backstop** because the writes run on the service-role client.

**Reachable vs RLS-capped, quantified:**
- **Genuinely reachable today, no RLS protection:** AUTHZ-SR-01, AUTHZ-SR-02. Exploit needs only a known victim UUID + any single business membership. This is the real exposure.
- **Latent, opens the instant a second coach is provisioned, no RLS protection:** the subscription-budgets route (AUTHZ-SUBBUDGET-01 / AUTHZ-HELPER-01 / AUTHZ-B — three re-verifications of one defect at `subscription-budgets/route.ts:152`) and the two consolidation mutation routes (`tenants/[connectionId]` = AUTHZ-CONSOL-TENANT-03; `forecasts/[forecastId]` = AUTHZ-CONSOL-FORECAST-02). All gate a service-role write on the *global* `role==='coach'` check instead of `assigned_coach_id`. Prod `system_roles` = 1 coach / 2 super_admin / 21 client, so today the sole coach legitimately manages the whole fleet and no boundary is crossed. One `INSERT` into `system_roles` (routine for a coaching platform) makes all of these live cross-client read/write/delete.
- **RLS-capped (wrong pattern, but protected):** the ~11 per-business finance/forecast routes that use the same global-`coach` fallback but run on the *auth-bound* client (AUTHZ-01 group / AUTHZ-HELPER-02). RLS's `auth_get_accessible_business_ids` scopes coaches to assigned businesses, so these are latent best-practice gaps only.

Net: the DB RLS hardening is doing real work and caps a whole class of sloppy inline authz — but it cannot save the ~5 routes that reach for the service-role key, and those are exactly where the exploitable holes are.

## 2. Ranked remediation plan

### Tier A — fix now, safe, no model dependency (reachable today by any authenticated user)

1. **AUTHZ-SR-01 — `goals/save/route.ts:101`.** Stop accepting `profileId` as a write key. Derive it server-side from the already-authorized `businessId` via `resolveBusinessProfileIds(admin, businessId)` (already imported for the KPI branch). If a `profileId` is passed at all, verify `profile.business_id === businessId` and reject on mismatch. Low risk — the KPI branch already does exactly this in the same file.
2. **AUTHZ-SR-02 — `team/remove-member/route.ts:78,96`.** Add `.eq('business_id', businessId)` to both the member `select` and the `delete` (or fetch-then-403 if `member.business_id !== businessId`). Purely additive scoping; cannot lock out a legitimate caller who is acting on their own business.

### Tier B — fix now, but requires verifying the assigned-coach model first (latent; opens on 2nd coach)

These change coach authorization, so confirm the `businesses.assigned_coach_id` model is populated for the live coach before tightening, or you will lock out the platform's one working coach. `verifyBusinessAccess` already implements the correct predicate, so the safest change is to *delegate to it* rather than hand-roll.

3. **subscription-budgets (`route.ts:152`) — one defect, three finding ids (AUTHZ-SUBBUDGET-01, AUTHZ-HELPER-01, AUTHZ-B).** Replace the global `role==='coach'||'super_admin'` clause in `authoriseBusinessAccess` with `businesses.assigned_coach_id === user.id` for the coach path (keep `super_admin` as the only global bypass), or call `verifyBusinessAccess()`. This is the highest-value Tier-B item: it guards GET/POST/DELETE (read, upsert, delete of another client's budgets), all on the service-role client.
4. **AUTHZ-CONSOL-TENANT-03 — `consolidation/tenants/[connectionId]/route.ts:106`.** After the role gate, resolve the connection's owning business (`xero_connections.business_id` is businesses-space) and require caller == that business's `assigned_coach_id` (or super_admin) before the `adminDb` update. Prevents cross-client edits to Xero connection flags (`is_active`, `include_in_consolidation`, `functional_currency`).
5. **AUTHZ-CONSOL-FORECAST-02 / AUTHZ-C — `consolidation/forecasts/[forecastId]/route.ts:146`.** Same fix: load the forecast's `business_id`, resolve dual-ID, verify assigned-coach/super_admin before the service-role `tenant_id` retag. (One verifier rated this MEDIUM — narrower blast radius, single `tenant_id` field — but the pattern and fix are identical to #4; do them together. The sibling `consolidation/businesses/[id]` route already shows the correct `.or()` owner/assigned_coach scoping to copy.)

### Tier C — hardening / correctness (no proven cross-tenant path)

6. **AUTHZ-02 / VALID-D — confirm `ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES` in prod (`with-schema.ts`).** The withSchema/withQuerySchema wrappers run observe-only by default; validation is inert unless the env var is set. Set it to `'*'` (or at minimum the id-bearing service-role routes). Until confirmed, treat each handler's own UUID checks as the only gate — which is why the consolidation routes' inline `UUID_REGEX` matters and should be adopted everywhere.
7. **AUTHZ-01 group / AUTHZ-HELPER-02 — the ~11 auth-bound routes with a global `role==='coach'` fallback** (`forecast/[id]` et al.). Standardize on `verifyBusinessAccess()` and delete the inline global-coach clause. RLS-capped today, so this is defense-in-depth, but it removes the latent footgun and makes the app layer correct without leaning on RLS.
8. **AUTHZ-A — `Xero/sync-all` POST.** Any authenticated user can trigger a sync for any business or the whole fleet. Gate `postHandler` via `verifyBusinessAccess`; restrict `all=true` to super_admin. (No data disclosure — a resource/side-effect issue.)
9. **Low/info:** AUTHZ-SR-03 (add `status='active'` to goals/save membership fallback), AUTHZ-SR-04 / ACTIVITY-LOGIN-07 (`activity-log/login` GET+POST — add `verifyBusinessAccess` on the client-supplied `business_id`), AUTHZ-HELPER-04 (forecast DELETE passes a `business_profiles.id` to `requireSectionPermission` — wrong id-space but fails *closed*, false-deny only), AUTHZ-HELPER-03 (section-permission gate ships LOG_ONLY — confirm intended), FXRATES-COACHGLOBAL-08 (fx-rates coach-global on a non-tenant table — acceptable, document). AUTHZ-03 / INJ-E (`.or()` template interpolation) was chased to ground on every instance — no attacker-controlled unvalidated value reaches a filter; UUID-validate before interpolation as cheap defense-in-depth.

## 3. Not covered by this audit

- **DB layer** (out of scope by design): RLS policy correctness, definer-RPC ACLs, cross-tenant DB guards — audited and hardened separately. This audit assumes those hold and only flags where the *app layer* bypasses them via the service-role client.
- **Session/JWT issuance internals** — Supabase Auth token minting, cookie signing, refresh-token rotation, session fixation. Only presence-of-session (`getUser()`) was checked, not the issuance mechanism.
- **Rate-limiting / brute-force / enumeration** beyond noting that the two IDOR paths depend on non-enumerable UUIDs; no audit of whether those UUIDs leak through other endpoints (reports, resolve, URLs) at a rate that makes enumeration practical.
- **Supabase Auth dashboard config** — email-confirmation, password policy, allowed redirect URLs, provider settings.
- **The one unverifiable prod fact:** whether `ZOD_ENFORCE_ROUTES` is actually set in Vercel prod env (finding VALID-D/AUTHZ-02). Read-only prod access confirmed only FK/PK/`system_roles` counts, not env vars.
- **Exhaustive line-by-line read of all ~74 service-role routes** — the ~15 taking a client-supplied business/forecast/connection id under a service-role query were read in full; the remainder were classified by import + gate pattern, not deep-read.
